findings.message: The new duplicate-guard `if broker in self.brokers` in `_add_broker` is unreachable: its only callers are `_init_setupable_` (list is guaranteed empty at that point) and `set_broker` (already guarded by `if self.brokers: raise SetupError(...)`). So the guard can never fire and adds dead code / an untested branch.
findings.suggestion: Either drop the guard (keep the single location of the `already has a broker` check in `set_broker`), or if the intent is to guard all future callers, add a test that exercises it directly (e.g. call `app._add_broker(b)` twice) so the branch is covered.

findings.message: `self.brokers: list[BrokerUsecase[Any, Any]] = []` annotates with `BrokerUsecase`, which is imported only under TYPE_CHECKING. This is safe in this codebase (the identical pattern already exists and runs fine in `faststream/specification/asyncapi/factory.py:40`), so no runtime NameError. Noting only for awareness.
findings.suggestion: No change required; optionally keep consistent with the existing factory pattern.

findings.message: No regression test was added asserting that `set_broker` propagates the app config to the broker via `_update_fd_config` (the exact behavior the issue reports). Existing tests still pass but would not catch a future re-break of this path.
findings.suggestion: Add a test in tests/application/test_delayed_broker.py asserting the app context/config is applied after `set_broker`, e.g. check `broker.config.fd_config.context['app'] is app` or that context injection into a handler works after a delayed `set_broker`.
